_comment: Noise-placement defaults per world type. Hand-authored (unlike
structure-groups.json, which is generated) — this is design intent, not
derived data. Read at boot by StructureGroupRegistry; a dimension config's
structures.noise / structures.radial / structureDensity override anything
here, per group.
Resolution order for a group's profile, most specific first:
1. structures.noise.<group>        (per-group override)
2. structures.noise                (string form: all groups)
3. structureDensity                (none kills noise entirely)
4. difficultyShifts                (mobMultiplier-driven)
5. types.<type>.profiles.<group>   (this file)
6. groupDefaults.<group>.profile   (this file)
Radial resolution is the same shape, with structures.radial taking a raw
10-point curve instead of a named one.
The base worlds resolve against the entries below by family: overworld ->
overworld, the_nether -> nether, the_end -> end, paradise_lost ->
paradise_lost:paradise_lost. Their files name no type (vanilla owns their
generator) and the mod supplies one; the Nether and the End additionally
carry a progression floor in scripts/check-noise-regression.py.
Placement is boot-re-read, not creation-time, so a change here reaches
newly generated chunks only — already-explored terrain keeps the
structures it has, and the seam is the same one a spacing change makes.

curves._comment: 10-point piecewise-linear weights, spawn (index 0) -> border (index 9). Multiplied into the noise before the threshold test, so 0.0 suppresses a band outright and 2.0 roughly doubles the hit rate there.

_comment: profile   — noise shape (natural | dense | sparse | cluster | none)
radial    — named curve from `curves`
exclusion — minimum chunks between two placements IN THIS GROUP. Groups
are independent, so a village and a ruin may sit adjacent;
two villages may not. Scaled by the profile's exclusion
multiplier (dense 0.6x, sparse 1.5x, cluster 0.4x).
SPACING for /locate probing is exclusion * 2, so each locate
cell holds at most one placement.
The spike gives an exclusion-per-RARITY table and also says all
structures in a group share the group's exclusion. Both cannot hold, and
per-group is the one that makes the placement well-defined (a single
NoiseStructurePlacement serves the whole group and has one exclusion
radius). Values below blend the concept spike's per-theme table with the
implementation spike's per-rarity table, keyed on each group's
characteristic rarity. Rarity still governs a set's SHARE of its group's
placements — that is where common-vs-endgame is expressed.

rarityShares._comment: Relative weight of a set within its group's placements. A group holding three `common` sets and one `rare` gives each common 8/25 of the placements and the rare 1/25. Overridden per dimension by structures.rarity.

_comment: Applied before the per-type table, after any explicit dimension config.
difficulty.mobMultiplier is the input. A dangerous world puts threat
everywhere and brings the prize within reach; a peaceful world has
neither. `hostileGroups` names the groups a peaceful world suppresses —
the same intent as the existing peaceful overlay dropping dungeon-theme
sets, expressed in group terms.
`groups` is the enabled set for the type. Biome filtering then removes
individual structures whose biome predicate does not intersect the
dimension's biome source, so a jungle multi_biome gets jungle temples
and not igloos without either being named here.
Every type in the roller's OVERWORLD_FAMILY / NETHER_FAMILY /
END_FAMILY has an entry, plus void, superflat, single_biome and
paradise_lost:paradise_lost. Types the spike did not list
(large_biomes, checkerboard, single_biome) are overworld-family and
take the overworld defaults.

amplified._comment: Dramatic terrain already carries the landscape, so landmarks are allowed to be a normal feature of it rather than a rare event.

cave._comment: No sky, no sea, no villages. Loot caches are the reward for going deep, so they run dense.

sky_islands._comment: Islands over void: nothing maritime, and the danger is the fall rather than the mobs.

nether._comment: Hostility is the ambient condition, not a destination — dungeons run at natural density and spread evenly rather than hiding at the border.

end._comment: End cities and their kin ARE the content — endgame runs at natural density here instead of sparse. Maritime covers the void-ship sets.

paradise_lost:paradise_lost._comment: Skylands: gentle, built, no hostile mega-content.

void._comment: No terrain to stand on. Nothing generates; a config may still force placements.

superflat._comment: Not rollable and never noise-placed — a flat world's structures are whatever its layers config allows.
